requirement_text: a secondary high school diploma (level 4 EQF) earned after at least 12 years of school attendance. For applicants with a secondary school diploma awarded after less than 12 years of school attendance: secondary high school diploma awarded after 11 years [...] + all first-year university exams completed with a passing grade or [...] 10 years [...] + all first and second-year university exams [...] or [...] 10 or 11 years [...] + a post secondary qualification [...] or [...] 10 or 11 years [...] + passing preparatory courses (Foundation Course) at an Italian university.
researcher_notes: Same 12-year national threshold documented in the Italy admissions-systems background doc, confirmed directly at institution level with the full set of compensatory routes for shorter systems. Politecnico publishes its own approved Foundation Course provider list (Ca' Foscari, Pavia, Pisa, Torino, La Sapienza, Siena, Parma, Tor Vergata, Brescia, Sassari, Campus Bio-Medico, plus art/design institutes IED/RUFA/NABA and LUISS/LUMSA), each tied to specific subject areas -- not a generic 'any Foundation Year' acceptance.

requirement_text: U.S. High School Diploma with at least 3 Advanced Placements (APs) with scores ranging from 3 to 5 in three different subjects [...] or British qualification: [...] International Advanced Level, if they certify that the student passed at least three subjects at an advanced level (A level) with a passing grade [...] or Scottish secondary high school diploma, with a passing grade in at least 3 Advanced Highers or, alternatively, 2 Advanced Highers and at least 4 Highers [...] or International Baccalaureate Diploma released by a school institution recognized by the International Baccalaureate Organisation (IBO).
researcher_notes: Named-qualification-specific admission routes (US AP, A-Level, Scottish Highers, IB), each with its own explicit passing structure.

requirement_text: For Countries where a national entrance examination for higher education admission is compulsory, applicants must upload a certificate attesting that the national admission test has been passed (for ex: YKS, Concurso Vestibular, Gao Kao - minimum score 400 for Marco Polo students, Pruebas de Selectividad, Veveosi Prosvasis, ecc).
researcher_notes: Explicitly names the required national exam by country -- Turkey's YKS, Brazil's Concurso Vestibular, China's Gao Kao (minimum 400 specifically for Marco Polo Project students), Spain's Pruebas de Selectividad, Greece's Panhellenic exams ('Veveosi Prosvasis') -- a genuinely useful cross-country reference list volunteered by an Italian institution's own page, not derived from the Italy background doc.

requirement_text: Passing the TIL admission test or submitting a SAT score (SAT is NOT VALID for Architecture). Specific requirements can be found in the Calls for application
researcher_notes: Per the brief's instruction to record test name/body: TIL (Politecnico di Torino's own test) or SAT (College Board) -- with an explicit named exception that SAT is not accepted for the Architecture programme specifically.

requirement_text: Admission to Politecnico does not automatically guarantee that you will obtain a visa. [...] If you are denied a visa, you will not be able to enrol at Politecnico di Torino. [...] Pre-enrollment is mandatory to obtain a type-D 'study visa'. The confirmation of eligibility does NOT replace the procedure on UNIVERSITALY.
researcher_notes: Independently confirms, at a second Italian institution, the same three-gate structure found at Sapienza (academic admission / visa issuance / final enrolment are three separate decisions, none guaranteeing the next) -- not a coincidence specific to one university, appears to be the shape of the national Universitaly system itself.
